import Lax977378.OuterContexts

/-!
---
title: Locality of the calculation without tags
type: lemma
---
At stage i+1 the exceptional region contains the radius-ρ(i+1) balls
around the previous exceptional region and the newly chosen endpoints.
An ordinary root therefore sees no current endpoint on its inspected ball,
and each recursive call at a ball vertex sees no previous exceptional tag.
-/
namespace Lax977378.TagSafety
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.OuterContexts

def radius : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | i+1 => radius i + (i+1)

axiom ordinaryCalls {c i} {G : Graph c} (previous endpoints current : Finset (Fin G.size))
    (covered : ∀ u ∈ previous ∪ endpoints, ∀ x, within G (radius (i+1)) u x → x ∈ current)
    {x} (ordinary : x ∉ current) {v} (hv : within G (i+1) x v) :
    v ∉ endpoints ∧ ∀ w, within G (radius i) v w → w ∉ previous

end Lax977378.TagSafety

statements.signature:
ordinaryCalls : ∀ {c i : Nat} {G : Lax977378.Logic.Graph c} (previous endpoints current : Finset (Fin G.size)),
  (∀ (u : Fin G.size),
      SetLike.instMembership.mem (Finset.instUnion.union previous endpoints) u →
        ∀ (x : Fin G.size),
          Lax977378.OuterContexts.within G (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius (instHAdd.hAdd i 1)) u x →
            SetLike.instMembership.mem current x) →
    ∀ {x : Fin G.size},
      Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem current x) →
        ∀ {v : Fin G.size},
          Lax977378.OuterContexts.within G (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) x v →
            And (Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem endpoints v))
              (∀ (w : Fin G.size),
                Lax977378.OuterContexts.within G (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius i) v w →
                  Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem previous w))

concepts.title: An independent order on a graph with the same window and coloured types
concepts.description:
Transport the exception names and endpoint roles through the finite window.
Elsewhere use the untagged coloured types realised on both graphs. These
data determine a target order with exactly the source spectrum.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax977378.TableFacts
import Lax977378.LocalCover
import Lax977378.CoverReplay
import Lax977378.MarkedSets

/-!
---
title: An independent order on a graph with the same window and coloured types
type: lemma
---
Transport the exception names and endpoint roles through the finite window.
Elsewhere use the untagged coloured types realised on both graphs. These
data determine a target order with exactly the source spectrum.
-/
namespace Lax977378.TargetOrder
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.OuterContexts Lax977378.RecordTests Lax977378.Planting
open Lax977378.SourceTables Lax977378.TagSafety

axiom targetOrder {c d K q p} (W A B : Graph c) (ha : A.Bounded d) (hb : B.Bounded d)
    (a : LinearOrder (Fin A.size)) (T : Nat → Table A a)
    (next : ∀ j < K, Follows j (T j) (T (j+1)))
    (κ : Fin A.size → Fin q) (kB : Fin B.size → Fin q)
    (base : ∀ x y, (T 0).part.block x = (T 0).part.block y ↔ x = y ∨
      x ∉ (T 0).exceptions ∧ y ∉ (T 0).exceptions ∧ κ x = κ y ∧ ∀ i, A.pred i x ↔ A.pred i y)
    (sep : ∀ x, Function.Injective (fun u : Ball A K x => (T 0).part.block u.val))
    (mark : Finset (Fin W.size)) (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size) (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size)
    (wy : Window W A (radius K+p) mark y) (wz : Window W B (radius K+p) mark z)
    (named : mark.image y = (T K).exceptions)
    (col : ∀ j, (∃ m ∈ mark, within W (radius K) m j) → κ (y j) = kB (z j))
    (seeds : List (Request c q))
    (typesA : ∀ x ∉ (T K).exceptions, ∃ s ∈ seeds, Realised s A (radius K) κ x)
    (typesB : ∀ w ∉ mark.image z, ∃ s ∈ seeds, Realised s B (radius K) kB w)
    (copiesA : ∀ s ∈ seeds, ∃ x ∉ (T K).exceptions, Realised s A (radius K) κ x)
    (copiesB : ∀ s ∈ seeds, ∃ w ∉ mark.image z, Realised s B (radius K) kB w) :
    ∃ b, spectrumAgrees A B a b K

end Lax977378.TargetOrder

statements.signature:

  A.Bounded d →
    B.Bounded d →
      ∀ (a : LinearOrder (Fin A.size)) (T : Nat → Lax977378.SourceTables.Table A a),
        (∀ (j : Nat), instLTNat.lt j K → Lax977378.SourceTables.Follows j (T j) (T (instHAdd.hAdd j 1))) →
          ∀ (κ : Fin A.size → Fin q) (kB : Fin B.size → Fin q),
            (∀ (x y : Fin A.size),
                Iff (Eq ((T 0).part.block x) ((T 0).part.block y))
                  (Or (Eq x y)
                    (And (Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (T 0).exceptions x))
                      (And (Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (T 0).exceptions y))
                        (And (Eq (κ x) (κ y)) (∀ (i : Fin c), Iff (A.pred i x) (A.pred i y))))))) →
              (∀ (x : Fin A.size), Function.Injective fun u => (T 0).part.block u.val) →
                ∀ (mark : Finset (Fin W.size)) (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size) (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size),
                  Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W A (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) p) mark y →
                    Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W B (instHAdd.hAdd (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) p) mark z →
                      Eq (Finset.image y mark) (T K).exceptions →
                        (∀ (j : Fin W.size),
                            (Exists fun m =>
                                And (SetLike.instMembership.mem mark m)
                                  (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) m j)) →
                              Eq (κ (y j)) (kB (z j))) →
                          ∀ (seeds : List (Lax977378.Planting.Request c q)),
                            (∀ (x : Fin A.size),
                                Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (T K).exceptions x) →
                                  Exists fun s =>
                                    And (List.instMembership.mem seeds s)
                                      (Lax977378.Planting.Realised s A (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) κ x)) →
                              (∀ (w : Fin B.size),
                                  Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (Finset.image z mark) w) →
                                    Exists fun s =>
                                      And (List.instMembership.mem seeds s)
                                        (Lax977378.Planting.Realised s B (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) kB w)) →
                                (∀ (s : Lax977378.Planting.Request c q),
                                    List.instMembership.mem seeds s →
                                      Exists fun x =>
                                        And (Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (T K).exceptions x))
                                          (Lax977378.Planting.Realised s A (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) κ x)) →
                                  (∀ (s : Lax977378.Planting.Request c q),
                                      List.instMembership.mem seeds s →
                                        Exists fun w =>
                                          And (Not (SetLike.instMembership.mem (Finset.image z mark) w))
                                            (Lax977378.Planting.Realised s B (Lax977378.TagSafety.radius K) kB w)) →
                                    Exists fun b => Lax977378.OuterContexts.spectrumAgrees A B a b K

concepts.title: Recovering the target exceptional vertices from one successful test
concepts.description:
The same unordered record identifies the exact low counts, the target rare
vertices, and a bijection between the source and target marked sets. Every
bounded-degree count threshold used for the source remains valid in the target.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax977378.SourceRecord

/-!
---
title: Recovering the target exceptional vertices from one successful test
type: lemma
---
The same unordered record identifies the exact low counts, the target rare
vertices, and a bijection between the source and target marked sets. Every
bounded-degree count threshold used for the source remains valid in the target.
-/
namespace Lax977378.TargetWindow
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.RecordTests Lax977378.CountParameters

axiom targetWindow {c n} (A B : Graph c) (D : TestData c) (types : Fin n → Pointed c)
    (v : Fin n → Nat) (t : Nat) (tcap : t ≤ D.cap)
    (counts : D.counts = List.ofFn (fun j => (types j,v j)))
    (freq : D.frequent = ((List.finRange n).filter (fun j => t ≤ v j)).map types)
    (y : Fin D.windowGraph.size → Fin A.size) (wy : Window D.windowGraph A D.windowRadius D.marked y)
    (pass : Passes D B) :
    (∀ j, v j = min D.cap (locations (types j) D.radius B).card) ∧
    (∀ j, t ≤ v j ↔ t ≤ (locations (types j) D.radius B).card) ∧
    ∃ z, Window D.windowGraph B D.windowRadius D.marked z ∧
      D.rare.image z = rareSet types D.radius B v t ∧
      ∃ e : (D.marked.image z) ≃ (D.marked.image y),
        ∀ j (hj : j ∈ D.marked), (e ⟨z j, Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ hj⟩).val = y j

end Lax977378.TargetWindow

  (types : Fin n → Lax977378.RecordTests.Pointed c) (v : Fin n → Nat) (t : Nat),
  instLENat.le t D.cap →
    Eq D.counts (List.ofFn fun j => { fst := types j, snd := v j }) →
      Eq D.frequent
          (List.map types (List.filter (fun j => Decidable.decide (instLENat.le t (v j))) (List.finRange n))) →
        ∀ (y : Fin D.windowGraph.size → Fin A.size),
          Lax977378.RecordTests.Window D.windowGraph A D.windowRadius D.marked y →
            Lax977378.RecordTests.Passes D B →
              And
                (∀ (j : Fin n),
                  Eq (v j) (instMinNat.min D.cap (Lax977378.CountParameters.locations (types j) D.radius B).card))
                (And
                  (∀ (j : Fin n),
                    Iff (instLENat.le t (v j))
                      (instLENat.le t (Lax977378.CountParameters.locations (types j) D.radius B).card))
                  (Exists fun z =>
                    And (Lax977378.RecordTests.Window D.windowGraph B D.windowRadius D.marked z)
                      (And (Eq (Finset.image z D.rare) (Lax977378.CountParameters.rareSet types D.radius B v t))
                        (Exists fun e =>
                          ∀ (j : Fin D.windowGraph.size) (hj : SetLike.instMembership.mem D.marked j),
                            Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe e ⟨z j, ⋯⟩).val (y j)))))

concepts.title: Uniform threshold for a finite list of type counts
concepts.description:
For a fixed number of counts we can choose a uniformly bounded positive
threshold. The threshold dominates a prescribed nondecreasing function of
the total of the counts strictly below it, including when some counts vanish.
concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Data.List.Basic
import Mathlib.Order.Monotone.Basic

/-!
---
title: Uniform threshold for a finite list of type counts
type: lemma
---
For a fixed number of counts we can choose a uniformly bounded positive
threshold. The threshold dominates a prescribed nondecreasing function of
the total of the counts strictly below it, including when some counts vanish.
-/
namespace Lax977378.Threshold

def rareTotal (t : Nat) (counts : List Nat) : Nat :=
  ((counts.filter (fun n => decide (n < t))).sum)

axiom uniformGap (N : Nat) (h : Nat → Nat) (mono : Monotone h) :
    ∃ U, ∀ counts : List Nat, counts.length ≤ N →
      ∃ t, 0 < t ∧ t ≤ U ∧ h (rareTotal t counts) ≤ t

end Lax977378.Threshold

statements.signature:

  Monotone h →
    Exists fun U =>
      ∀ (counts : List Nat),
        instLENat.le counts.length N →
          Exists fun t =>
            And (instLTNat.lt 0 t)
              (And (instLENat.le t U) (instLENat.le (h (Lax977378.Threshold.rareTotal t counts)) t))

concepts.title: Transport of a refinement to an independently ordered graph
concepts.description:
A target vertex is assigned a source representative by the local calculation.
Every source child row must be hit. Endpoint children are singletons, and
the correspondence recognises the two chosen target endpoints. Ordering
the target by the representative's child row then enforces the recorded
endpoints, in every compatible order. Ball correspondences allow the previous
table to compute the new outer contexts across the two graphs.

import Lax977378.Stage

/-!
---
title: Transport of a refinement to an independently ordered graph
type: lemma
---
A target vertex is assigned a source representative by the local calculation.
Every source child row must be hit. Endpoint children are singletons, and
the correspondence recognises the two chosen target endpoints. Ordering
the target by the representative's child row then enforces the recorded
endpoints, in every compatible order. Ball correspondences allow the previous
table to compute the new outer contexts across the two graphs.
-/
namespace Lax977378.Transport
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.Blocks Lax977378.OuterContexts Lax977378.Stage

axiom transport {c d n m i} (A B : Graph c) (ha : A.Bounded d) (hb : B.Bounded d)
    (a : LinearOrder (Fin A.size))
    (P : @Partition (Fin A.size) (Fin n) a inferInstance)
    (C : @Partition (Fin A.size) (Fin m) a inferInstance)
    (hom : ∀ x y, C.block x = C.block y → same A A a a (i+1) x y)
    (parent : ∀ x y, C.block x = C.block y → P.block x = P.block y)
    (singleF : ∀ x j, C.block x = C.block (P.first j) → x = P.first j)
    (singleL : ∀ x j, C.block x = C.block (P.last j) → x = P.last j)
    (rep : Fin B.size → Fin A.size) (hit : Function.Surjective (C.block ∘ rep))
    (f l : Fin n → Fin B.size) (rf : ∀ j, rep (f j) = P.first j)
    (rl : ∀ j, rep (l j) = P.last j)
    (uf : ∀ j z, rep z = P.first j → z = f j)
    (ul : ∀ j z, rep z = P.last j → z = l j)
    (lower : ∀ (b : LinearOrder (Fin B.size)), Compatible b (P.block ∘ rep) →
      ∀ x z, P.block x = P.block (rep z) → same A B a b i x z)
    (balls : ∀ z, ∃ h : Ball A (i+1) (rep z) ≃ Ball B (i+1) z,
      (∀ u, u.val = rep z ↔ (h u).val = z) ∧
      (∀ u v, A.edge u.val v.val ↔ B.edge (h u).val (h v).val) ∧
      Function.Injective (fun u : Ball A (i+1) (rep z) => P.block u.val) ∧
      (∀ u, P.block u.val = P.block (rep (h u).val)) ∧
      (∀ u, u.val = P.first (P.block u.val) ↔ (h u).val = f (P.block (rep (h u).val))) ∧
      (∀ u, u.val = P.last (P.block u.val) ↔ (h u).val = l (P.block (rep (h u).val)))) :
    ∀ (b : LinearOrder (Fin B.size)), Compatible b (C.block ∘ rep) →
      (∃ Q : @Partition (Fin B.size) (Fin n) b inferInstance,
        Q.block = P.block ∘ rep ∧ Q.first = f ∧ Q.last = l) ∧
      (∀ x z, C.block x = C.block (rep z) → same A B a b (i+1) x z) ∧
      spectrumAgrees A B a b (i+1)

end Lax977378.Transport

statements.signature:

  A.Bounded d →
    B.Bounded d →
      ∀ (a : LinearOrder (Fin A.size)) (P : Lax977378.Blocks.Partition (Fin A.size) (Fin n))
        (C : Lax977378.Blocks.Partition (Fin A.size) (Fin m)),
        (∀ (x y : Fin A.size),
            Eq (C.block x) (C.block y) → Lax977378.OuterContexts.same A A a a (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) x y) →
          (∀ (x y : Fin A.size), Eq (C.block x) (C.block y) → Eq (P.block x) (P.block y)) →
            (∀ (x : Fin A.size) (j : Fin n), Eq (C.block x) (C.block (P.first j)) → Eq x (P.first j)) →
              (∀ (x : Fin A.size) (j : Fin n), Eq (C.block x) (C.block (P.last j)) → Eq x (P.last j)) →
                ∀ (rep : Fin B.size → Fin A.size),
                  Function.Surjective (Function.comp C.block rep) →
                    ∀ (f l : Fin n → Fin B.size),
                      (∀ (j : Fin n), Eq (rep (f j)) (P.first j)) →
                        (∀ (j : Fin n), Eq (rep (l j)) (P.last j)) →
                          (∀ (j : Fin n) (z : Fin B.size), Eq (rep z) (P.first j) → Eq z (f j)) →
                            (∀ (j : Fin n) (z : Fin B.size), Eq (rep z) (P.last j) → Eq z (l j)) →
                              (∀ (b : LinearOrder (Fin B.size)),
                                  Lax977378.Stage.Compatible b (Function.comp P.block rep) →
                                    ∀ (x : Fin A.size) (z : Fin B.size),
                                      Eq (P.block x) (P.block (rep z)) → Lax977378.OuterContexts.same A B a b i x z) →
                                (∀ (z : Fin B.size),
                                    Exists fun h =>
                                      And
                                        (∀ (u : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) (rep z)),
                                          Iff (Eq u.val (rep z)) (Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val z))
                                        (And
                                          (∀ (u v : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) (rep z)),
                                            Iff (A.edge u.val v.val)
                                              (B.edge (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val
                                                (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h v).val))
                                          (And (Function.Injective fun u => P.block u.val)
                                            (And
                                              (∀ (u : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) (rep z)),
                                                Eq (P.block u.val) (P.block (rep (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val)))
                                              (And
                                                (∀ (u : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) (rep z)),
                                                  Iff (Eq u.val (P.first (P.block u.val)))
                                                    (Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val
                                                      (f (P.block (rep (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val)))))
                                                (∀ (u : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) (rep z)),
                                                  Iff (Eq u.val (P.last (P.block u.val)))
                                                    (Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val
                                                      (l (P.block (rep (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h u).val)))))))))) →
                                  ∀ (b : LinearOrder (Fin B.size)),
                                    Lax977378.Stage.Compatible b (Function.comp C.block rep) →
                                      And
                                        (Exists fun Q =>
                                          And (Eq Q.block (Function.comp P.block rep))
                                            (And (Eq Q.first f) (Eq Q.last l)))
                                        (And
                                          (∀ (x : Fin A.size) (z : Fin B.size),
                                            Eq (C.block x) (C.block (rep z)) →
                                              Lax977378.OuterContexts.same A B a b (instHAdd.hAdd i 1) x z)
                                          (Lax977378.OuterContexts.spectrumAgrees A B a b (instHAdd.hAdd i 1)))

import Lax977378.RecordTests

/-!
---
title: Exact distances in the record's exceptional window
type: lemma
---
A record names the entire radius-$(\rho+p)$ neighbourhood of its exceptional
set. Starting within distance $\rho$ of that set, every ambient path of length
at most $p$ can be read in the named induced graph. The conclusion includes
both the vertices reached and their distances up to the specified radius.
-/
namespace Lax977378.Window
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.OuterContexts Lax977378.RecordTests

axiom exactBall {c ρ p : Nat} {W G : Graph c} {mark : Finset (Fin W.size)}
    {y : Fin W.size → Fin G.size} (hw : RecordTests.Window W G (ρ+p) mark y)
    {u : Fin W.size} (near : ∃ m ∈ mark, within W ρ m u)
    (r : Nat) (hr : r ≤ p) (z : Fin G.size) :
    within G r (y u) z ↔ ∃ v, within W r u v ∧ y v = z

end Lax977378.Window

statements.signature:
exactBall : ∀ {c ρ p : Nat} {W G : Lax977378.Logic.Graph c} {mark : Finset (Fin W.size)} {y : Fin W.size → Fin G.size},
  Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W G (instHAdd.hAdd ρ p) mark y →
    ∀ {u : Fin W.size},
      (Exists fun m => And (SetLike.instMembership.mem mark m) (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W ρ m u)) →
        ∀ (r : Nat),
          instLENat.le r p →
            ∀ (z : Fin G.size),
              Iff (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within G r (y u) z)
                (Exists fun v => And (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W r u v) (Eq (y v) z))

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax977378.TargetWindow
import Lax977378.Window

/-!
---
title: Transporting the exceptional precolouring to a passing graph
type: lemma
---
Only the inner neighbourhood of the marked set is prescribed. Its colours
are proper in the target graph power because each relevant path stays in
the larger window. The number of prescribed vertices is bounded using the
degree bound, independently of the ambient graph size.
-/
namespace Lax977378.WindowColour
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.OuterContexts Lax977378.RecordTests Lax977378.Planting

axiom precolour {c d q r p} (W A B : Graph c) (hd : B.Bounded d) (mark : Finset (Fin W.size))
    (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size) (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size)
    (wy : Window W A (r+p) mark y) (wz : Window W B (r+p) mark z)
    (κ : Fin A.size → Fin q) (proper : ProperOn A p Finset.univ κ) (nonempty : 0 < q) :
    ∃ (P : Finset (Fin B.size)) (paint : Fin B.size → Fin q),
      P.card ≤ mark.card*(d+1)^r ∧ ProperOn B p P paint ∧
      (∀ j, (∃ m ∈ mark, within W r m j) → z j ∈ P ∧ paint (z j) = κ (y j))

end Lax977378.WindowColour

statements.signature:
precolour : ∀ {c d q r p : Nat} (W A B : Lax977378.Logic.Graph c),
  B.Bounded d →
    ∀ (mark : Finset (Fin W.size)) (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size) (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size),
      Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W A (instHAdd.hAdd r p) mark y →
        Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W B (instHAdd.hAdd r p) mark z →
          ∀ (κ : Fin A.size → Fin q),
            Lax977378.Planting.ProperOn A p Finset.univ κ →
              instLTNat.lt 0 q →
                Exists fun P =>
                  Exists fun paint =>
                    And (instLENat.le P.card (instHMul.hMul mark.card (instHPow.hPow (instHAdd.hAdd d 1) r)))
                      (And (Lax977378.Planting.ProperOn B p P paint)
                        (∀ (j : Fin W.size),
                          (Exists fun m =>
                              And (SetLike.instMembership.mem mark m) (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W r m j)) →
                            And (SetLike.instMembership.mem P (z j)) (Eq (paint (z j)) (κ (y j)))))

concepts.title: Corresponding recursive balls inside a common named window
concepts.description:
Two realisations of the same window identify the full balls around
corresponding interior vertices. The identification respects every vertex
name in the window, including on the boundary of the inspected ball.
concepts.sourceText:
import Lax977378.Window

/-!
---
title: Corresponding recursive balls inside a common named window
type: lemma
---
Two realisations of the same window identify the full balls around
corresponding interior vertices. The identification respects every vertex
name in the window, including on the boundary of the inspected ball.
-/
namespace Lax977378.WindowMap
open Lax977378.Logic Lax977378.OuterContexts Lax977378.RecordTests

axiom matchBall {c s p r} (W A B : Graph c) (mark : Finset (Fin W.size))
    (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size) (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size)
    (wy : Window W A (s+p) mark y) (wz : Window W B (s+p) mark z)
    (u : Fin W.size) (hu : ∃ m ∈ mark, within W s m u) (hr : r ≤ p) :
    ∃ h : Ball A r (y u) ≃ Ball B r (z u),
      (∀ v j, v.val = y j ↔ (h v).val = z j) ∧
      (∀ v, ∃ j, within W r u j ∧ v.val = y j ∧ (h v).val = z j) ∧
      (∀ v w, A.edge v.val w.val ↔ B.edge (h v).val (h w).val)

end Lax977378.WindowMap

statements.signature:
matchBall : ∀ {c s p r : Nat} (W A B : Lax977378.Logic.Graph c) (mark : Finset (Fin W.size)) (y : Fin W.size → Fin A.size)
  (z : Fin W.size → Fin B.size),
  Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W A (instHAdd.hAdd s p) mark y →
    Lax977378.RecordTests.Window W B (instHAdd.hAdd s p) mark z →
      ∀ (u : Fin W.size),
        (Exists fun m => And (SetLike.instMembership.mem mark m) (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W s m u)) →
          instLENat.le r p →
            Exists fun h =>
              And
                (∀ (v : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A r (y u)) (j : Fin W.size),
                  Iff (Eq v.val (y j)) (Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h v).val (z j)))
                (And
                  (∀ (v : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A r (y u)),
                    Exists fun j =>
                      And (Lax977378.OuterContexts.within W r u j)
                        (And (Eq v.val (y j)) (Eq (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h v).val (z j))))
                  (∀ (v w : Lax977378.OuterContexts.Ball A r (y u)),
                    Iff (A.edge v.val w.val)
                      (B.edge (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h v).val (EquivLike.toFunLike.coe h w).val)))

proofs.description:
Compose the first ball map with the inverse of the second. Lower calls at
corresponding ball vertices compare through their common target vertex.

The radius ball contains its centre and the rooted map sends it to the
other centre. Its child call reduces the rank while keeping both roots.

The cardinality of a ball increases by a factor of at most $d+1$ per step.
Number the actual vertices of the ball, transport their edges and unary
predicates, and use that numbering as the witness for its catalogue entry.

Pair every bounded unordered test with every possible set of final labels.
Keep the pairs with universal replay. The source graph's own witness lies
in this list, and membership gives replay on each target independently.
Global invariance restricts to every bounded-degree class.

Number the realised initial names. An equal name on two vertices of a
K-ball gives equal auxiliary colours, while the path through the centre
has length at most 2K. Proper colouring forces the vertices to coincide.

Index requests by a catalogue index and an embedding of its named vertices
into the palette. A realised ball inherits such an embedding since any two
of its vertices have distance at most twice its radius.

First fix the catalogue and its number of coloured requests. Choose the
frequency gap with room for the entire excluded set and one more realisation
of every request than there can be exceptions.

Use a pointed ordered ball isomorphism for each introduced cluster. Its
remaining radius covers all further guarded continuations. A child root
matches the comparisons to every vertex of its parent's ball, including
vertices that have not yet been played. The induction follows the CFO grammar.

Record all numberings of the rooted ball. Alongside the ball, each numbering
records the set of lower labels and order positions realised in the graph.
Transporting a numbering along a context isomorphism preserves these data.
Conversely a common numbered description supplies the required isomorphism.

An injection of the requested number of indices into the set of occurrences
is equivalent to the corresponding cardinality bound.

Choose thresholds after fixing the catalogue, so their growth function can
include the number of palette assignments for that very catalogue.

Take the least eligible threshold for each vector. Unique type membership
partitions the rare vertices into disjoint fibres, whose cardinalities are
exactly the unsaturated low entries of the vector.

Reverse coverage gives a witness at every source vertex. Compare that witness
to the chosen representative at the same target. They agree on the source
row at every lower level. The full root tag isolates each named endpoint.

Order first by block, then by endpoint position, and use the original vertex
number to break ties among the middle vertices. A coincident first and last
can occur precisely in a singleton block under the stated hypothesis.

At most the cardinality of the exceptional set is lost on taking the
difference. Choose two distinct surviving centres in the requested block.

Colour one as-yet unrestricted vertex with a colour outside the image of
its neighbourhood, retaining the colours of all previously fixed vertices.

Enumerate the union of the marked balls and pull the graph relations back
along the enumeration. Its inverse names exactly the marked and rare vertices.

Enumerate the two relation tables and both marked subsets on each possible
window size, the capped vector and the subset of frequent indices.

Enumerate every subset of the finite set of unary labels. Conjoin,
for each label, either an existential occurrence sentence or its negation.

For a witness between the endpoints, monotonicity places its block
between the two endpoint blocks inclusively. Conversely use the first
vertex of an intervening block, or the appropriate endpoint of a boundary block.

Upon descending to a named vertex in the inspected ball, increase the allowed
distance from the marked set by the current rank. The radius left in the
window is precisely the radius for the child call.

The outer slack ensures ambient distances are read exactly. Only inner
vertex data are consulted. At a recursive call the increased distance
allowance exactly offsets the reduction of the remaining inspection radius.

Two copies of a coloured request give an untagged comparison by their
common numbering. Named exceptional vertices instead use the inner window
with the recorded data. The argument works from either graph.

The lower calls determine all parent rows on the ball, including the root
row. Endpoint roles and the common preceding table then determine the new
context. Apply the rule defining the child groups.

Start at the common name of the exceptional vertex or endpoint. Lift the
target path, map it to the source, and apply the source covering condition.

The two ball vertices are both interior at this stage and both ordinary at
the previous stage. Induct on the remaining rank at that pair of vertices.

For a prefix use the first vertex of the boundary block, and for a suffix
use its last vertex. A block strictly on the appropriate side contributes
all its vertices.

Choose one occurrence outside the union of the forbidden balls, prescribe its
colours and include its whole ball in the next excluded set. The uniform
bound budgets for this increase on every request. Extend the resulting
partial colouring on the graph power after the final request.

Choose the growth allowance before taking the frequency gap. Extract the
source record from a colouring with reserves. On every passing target copy
the inner window colouring, plant the same frequent requests, and realise
the recorded spectrum using the independent target order.

Compile bounded graph distance recursively, quantify the vertices of the
finite diagram simultaneously, and use a universal vertex variable for exact
window coverage and exact coverage of rare vertices. Positive and negative
occurrence tests give counts up to the cap.

Transfer each interval witness in its own block. If that block also contains
a ball vertex, choose the corresponding vertex, first vertex or last vertex,
according to the side on which the witness must lie. Every other comparison
is fixed by the common order of the block indices.

Select the first-successful-test formulas with a positive witness in the class and disjoin them.
The ordered comparison and order invariance make each successful test
homogeneous for the chosen sentence.

Choose an order for each entry and each passing graph. A vertex label in
either graph belongs to the final table and is therefore realised in the
other graph under its independently chosen order.

Use the fixed window map on the exceptional set. Elsewhere choose any
ordinary source witness of the coloured type. Constancy on an ordinary type
turns coverage of types into coverage of child blocks.

Aligned lists give at least m realising centres for each request. Separation
makes the centres distinct, so they cannot all lie in the later exceptional set.

Induct on the rank, for every compatible target order. At a ball vertex the
recursive comparison and the fixed representative meet the same target call.
The source name is therefore the same. Endpoint fibres are singletons, so
the target endpoints read from their preimages have precisely the given roles.

The union of the previously forbidden vertices and one new forbidden ball
costs at most $H$ extra vertices. The induction therefore has enough space for
all the remaining requests.

Extract the window only after the final source order and all its tables have
been obtained. Monotonicity of the exceptional sets places every rare vertex
in that window, with the very same names as in the existential test.

Choose endpoints in every nonempty row. Enlarge the exceptional set by taking
the balls around it and the endpoints, then apply refinement. A child row
stays inside its parent, so separation on the full inspection ball persists.

Choose endpoints of the final rows and a compatible order. At each previous
level the history supplies a parent partition in this very order, including
its recorded extrema. Induction assembles the complete sequence.

Compute ordinary labels in one order with the chosen endpoints. Number the
realised child keys in increasing order. Every order respecting those keys
preserves the parent endpoints, so the preceding table computes the same
outer label at each vertex in every compatible order.

Each old exception and each new endpoint belongs to its own ball. For
separation, project a child row equality back to the initial rows and embed
the inspected ball in the K-ball. The child group rule gives homogeneity.

A path from a lower call to a previously exceptional vertex, followed in
reverse back to the root, would put the root in the current exceptional set.

Use a source vertex number only for vertices already exceptional at the
current stage. The target reads that number through its window name. Matching
full tags then isolates each endpoint in both graphs.

Read each capped count from its conjunct. Both marked sets have an injective
enumeration by the same window names.

Distinct child rows compare as in the source order. The first and last child
rows of each parent isolate their target endpoints. Apply the block evaluation
lemma at a representative, then use homogeneity of its source child row.

Two patterns occurring at the same vertex have numberings onto the same
ambient ball. Their root-preserving change of numbering transports an
occurrence on any graph. Retaining one representative of each such class
therefore partitions the vertices of every bounded-degree graph.

Start with the threshold $b=1+h(0)$. If a count is below $b$, remove it
and apply induction to the remaining counts with the allowance $b$ added
to their rare total. This bounds the effect of putting the count back.

For the reverse passage from the ambient graph, lift the path one edge at a
time. Each next vertex is still within the radius covered by the window, so
it has a name there. The induced diagram reflects the final edge.

Pull back a target path of length at most p from its first named vertex into
the window. Mapping that path into the source shows that the transported
colours must differ.

Both ambient balls are enumerated by the same inner ball of the window.
Compose the two enumerations and use the induced diagrams for edges.
